environmental.surge-protection: differential mode 2 kV, common mode 4 kV

features.layer: L3 (static routing, ERPS ring recovery 20 ms or less)
features.optics-sfp-plus: vendor optics listed under AurCore Accessories - AOM10M-S300 (10G, multimode, 300 m) and AOM10S-K10 (10G, single-mode, 10 km), with AOM01M-S550 and AOM01S-K10 at 1G; the datasheet states no compatibility list or third-party policy

management.interfaces: console, Telnet, SSH, SNMP v1/v2c/v3, web, ACC/ACN cloud

physical.accessories: two pluggable terminal plugs (power and relay), console cable
physical.dimensions-in: 5.71 x 4.33 x 3.30 (L x W x H, datasheet)

configs.description: AIS4001 industrial switch, 8x GbE and 4x 10G SFP+, L3, dual 12-55 V DC
configs.name: base

gaps.wanted: A dimensioned drawing or the in-box quick installation guide. Nothing published gives the bevel, the DIN clip's position or the top-face layout; they are photo-measured or estimated (see provenance). AurCore support or a reseller holds the guide.
The unit's weight; the datasheet gives none.
Confirmation of the port numbering read from the faceplate's arrows (see provenance sfp-numbering); a unit, or the switch's own port table against a seated optic, settles it.
A lamped RJ45 cell with 11.5 mm between its lamps on an 11 mm column; the library's nearest puts them 8.3 mm apart.

`attrs.platform.cpu`; one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in `attrs.environmental` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on port groups gbe, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

bevel.note: photo-measured - the housing is an octagon in section: the four edges that run from the port face to the back are cut off, which is what the user and the photographs call its wedge. The front's silhouette (front image, 4.407 px/mm) narrows 10.9 mm at its top and bottom rows and reaches full width 16.3 mm in, at every corner; the four product images give identical silhouettes, quantised to 1.8 mm by the image's mask, so 11 and 16 are good to about two millimetres. The video (0:31-0:41) shows these cuts running the whole depth. THE GREY BANDS BESIDE THE LEGEND PLATE ARE BEVELS TOO, which a first draft of this model read as flat casting and the maintainer corrected from the explorer: in the video's three-quarter frames (0:29-0:33, and the render at 0:46) the band right of the plate is lit as its own plane and its top edge slants up to meet the top face, and the back face (0:32) carries the same band between the plates and the fins. So the four edges between the front or back and the finned sides are bevelled as well, 12.6 mm across the face - the dark plate is 58.4 of the 83.8 mm, measured on the straight-on front - and taken at 45 degrees, because no view shows how far back along the side the bevel runs. The back is taken to match the front.

bottom-layout.note: estimated - the underside is not photographed. Drawn as plain casting, the bevels strips at its sides; registered as a gap.

chassis.note: datasheet - 'Dimension (L*W*H) 5.71 x 4.33 x 3.30 in'. The letters are not width, height and depth: the straight-on front reads 0.587 wide-to-tall against 3.30/5.71 = 0.578, so L (145.0 mm) is the face's height as the unit hangs on the rail, H (83.8) its width and W (110.0) the depth from the port face to the DIN face.

front-layout.note: photo-measured on the straight-on AIS4001 front image at 4.407 px/mm (Gate 1: the face's own width agrees with the datasheet to 1.5 percent; the datasheet's front is the same artwork). Jack lamps located by colour; columns at x 23.85 and 45.2, rows on a 15.57 mm pitch from y 43.2; SFP+ block x 22.2-47.8, rows from y 106.8 and 122.1. Jacks are drawn with the lamped ganged cell turned 90/270 so the keyways face out; its lamps are 8.3 mm apart against the jacks' 11.5, the closest library cell that fits the 11 mm column. The console is the bare ganged cell, turned the same way. Cages are std/sfp@1 on their side; each SFP lamp is a small dash drawn with common/led-rect-sm@1 turned 90.

lamps.note: photo-measured - each jack has ONE lamp, green, at its top (the PoE builds add an amber one below it), and the colour key names only LINK/ACT; drawn with common/rj45-ganged-link@1, the right-hand column drawn with its lamp-right skin so its lamp also lands at the top.

power.note: datasheet - 'Power Supply DC 12-55 V'; 'Idling: 12V 5.40W / 55V 6.05W'; 'Full load: 12V 12.25W / 55V 12.10W'. power-max-w takes the highest figure (12.25 W); no ambient is stated with any of them. The supply is not included ('the power supply is excluded from the package').

rear-layout.note: estimated - the back render is foreshortened top to bottom; widths are taken as fractions of the face on the same image row, heights as fractions of 145 mm. Two wall plates (upper with its screws above the keyholes, lower with them below) and the DIN clip between them, centred. The DIN rail's centre line lies about 79 mm from the top of this face.

relay-orientation.note: photo-measured - the two-position RELAY header is placed turned 90, its two contacts running front to back, parallel to the five of the power header, with its keyed, open side toward the RELAY legend as the power header's is toward the POWER legend. Read off the AurCore product video (frames at 0:34 and 1:02, the AIS4001P top face close up) and the vendor's AIS4001P and AIS2001 product images 2 (three-quarter) and 3 (back render), which show the same on both housings. It is placed at the centre it had unturned, 1.0 left of the old `at` because the header is now 12.16 wide, the Phoenix Contact MSTBA 2,5/ 2-G-5,08 width (#804).

sfp-numbering.note: photo-measured - the gold strip reads, top to bottom, an up-pointing triangle and 9, a lamp, a down-pointing triangle and 10, a lamp, up 11, a lamp, down 12, a lamp, in text turned to read down the face. Up in that text points away from the strip, so 9 and 11 are the right-hand column and 10 and 12 the left, top row first.

side-layout.note: estimated - from the video (0:37-0:41, 0:55) and the three-quarter image: both sides are fins running front to back, with a recessed channel and a raised badge plate carrying the wordmark on the right side. The left side is not photographed square on and is drawn as fins only.

silkscreen.note: photo-measured - legends transcribed from the AIS4001 front image: Reset, SYS, PWR; Fast Ring and SCP with leaders to switches 1 and 2; CONSOLE; the port numbers as printed; LINK/ACT under its colour key (no PoE key on this build); the summary line '8 x GE | 4 x 10GE SFP+ | L3'. The AURCORE wordmark is printed as text: its A is drawn as a chevron mark, which is not reproduced (no logo marks).

sources.note: vendor datasheet (AIS4001 Data Sheet 1.0, 3 pages: spec table, and an annotated front and back figure that is the same artwork as the product images); the product page's three images (straight-on front, three-quarter front-top-right, and a back render raised to show the top face), 1000 px; and the vendor's AIS4000 Series video (YouTube MfK6WpjLsA8, 1080p), whose footage at 0:28-1:02 is a real AIS4001P, the same housing - the top, back and sides here are that unit's, with the AIS4001's own power legend. No hardware guide or drawing is published (the Download Center holds the CLI, ACC and ACN manuals only).

top-layout.note: estimated - no straight-on top view exists. Positions are fractions of the top face in the back render (image 3, raised about 35 degrees), corrected with the parts' own sizes: the five-way power header (Phoenix MSTB-GF family, 35.56 mm) runs front to back with its pole legend '1 + - earth + - 2' on one side and POWER:12-55V DC on the other (read off this build's back render), pole 1 at the rear; the RELAY header and the ground screw with its earth symbol are near the front edge. The video (1:00-1:02) confirms every part and legend close up but not their places on the face. Good to a few millimetres.
